_comment: Pinned FFmpeg builds, one per Tauri target triple.
Pinning is not bureaucracy here: three lab machines must encode identically,
and two different FFmpeg builds can differ in default x264 tuning, in which
input pixel formats they negotiate, and in how -fps_mode cfr rounds. The
version string below is written into every recording manifest, so 'were these
two sessions produced the same way?' is answerable after the fact.
sha256 starts as null. Run `npm run ffmpeg -- --pin` once per target to
download, print, and write the real checksum back into this file. After that
every fetch verifies against it and a silently-rotated upstream build fails
loudly instead of drifting into the data.
macOS entries have not been exercised on real hardware yet — the lab Mac is
flagged as unverified across the repo's notes. Expect to adjust these URLs on
the first macOS build (Alexander, 2026-08-11).
KNOWN GAP, stated rather than left to be discovered (2026-09-12): Windows and
macOS are NOT on the same FFmpeg. Windows is pinned to 9.0.1 with a checksum;
both macOS entries are 7.1 and still unpinned (sha256: null). So the guarantee
at the top of this file — every lab machine on one encoder — currently holds
across the Windows machines only. All conversation recording happens on the
Windows room computers, so no study data is affected today, but a Mac used for
a session would produce files this manifest cannot vouch for. Closing it means
finding a 9.0.1 macOS build and running `--pin` on a Mac; until then
ffmpegVersion is declared per target so the smoke test compares against the
truth instead of warning on every macOS fetch, which is how a real warning
gets ignored.

x86_64-pc-windows-msvc._note: Pinned to gyan.dev's versioned package URL, not the rolling ffmpeg-release-essentials.zip. The rolling URL changes contents the moment upstream publishes anything, which broke every CI build here between 2026-08-30 and 2026-09-12 with a checksum mismatch — the pin working exactly as intended, but on a URL guaranteed to trip it. The versioned URL keeps serving these bytes until gyan prunes the package, at which point the fetch fails loudly and someone re-pins on purpose. (An earlier note here said gyan keeps no per-version URL. It does: /builds/packages/ffmpeg-<version>-essentials_build.zip.)
x86_64-pc-windows-msvc._repin_2026_09_12: 9.0 -> 9.0.1, forced because gyan had already pruned the 9.0 package (404) so the old build was no longer fetchable at all. Checked rather than assumed: encoding the same deterministic source with both builds at the lab's real settings gives a BYTE-IDENTICAL h264 bitstream under h264_qsv, and a 0.7% larger one under libx264 (the bundled x264 changed). Every lab machine records on a hardware encoder, so recordings are unaffected; only the software fallback would differ, and the encoder plus FFmpeg version are written into every recording manifest either way.
